name: Applied Chemistry
tagline: Real-world applications of chemistry in agriculture, industry, and daily life.
seo_title: Applied Chemistry — paper summaries, news & innovations | Chemisters
seo_description: Follow Chemisters Applied Chemistry on LinkedIn and Facebook: paper summaries, news and innovations in agricultural chemistry, water treatment, coatings, detergents and everyday products.

definition.lead: Applied chemistry puts chemical knowledge to work on practical problems: cleaner water, better crops, safer products and longer-lasting materials.
definition.body: It spans agriculture, cosmetics, paints, detergents, textiles, construction and countless everyday products. Where basic research asks 'why?', applied chemistry asks 'how do we make this work, at a price people can pay?'

timeline.title: Vulcanized rubber
timeline.text: Charles Goodyear heats rubber with sulfur.
timeline.why: Made rubber stable enough for tyres and seals.

timeline.title: Agricultural chemistry
timeline.text: Justus von Liebig publishes his book on chemistry applied to agriculture.
timeline.why: Explained plant nutrition and inspired mineral fertilizers.

timeline.title: Mauveine
timeline.text: William Perkin's synthetic dye launches an industry.

timeline.title: Chlorinated drinking water
timeline.text: Jersey City in the US starts continuous chlorination of its public water supply.
timeline.why: Sharply reduced waterborne diseases such as typhoid.

timeline.title: IUPAC
timeline.text: The International Union of Pure and Applied Chemistry is founded.
timeline.why: Common names, symbols and standards for chemists worldwide.

timeline.title: DDT's insecticidal action
timeline.text: Paul Müller discovers that DDT kills insects; it is later restricted for its environmental persistence.
timeline.why: Nobel Prize in Medicine in 1948, and a lesson in unintended consequences.

timeline.title: Synthetic laundry detergent
timeline.text: Procter & Gamble launches Tide, a synthetic detergent with phosphate builders.
timeline.why: Detergents replaced soap for washing clothes.

quiz.q: Why do some sunscreens contain zinc oxide or titanium dioxide?
quiz.explain: Fine particles block both UVA and UVB.

quiz.q: In a paint, the binder is…
options: The film-forming polymer that holds the pigment to the surface
The coloured powder that gives the paint its shade
The solvent that evaporates after the paint is applied
The dye dissolved in water that soaks into the wall
quiz.explain: Pigment gives colour; binder gives adhesion and durability.

quiz.q: Why is DDT restricted today, despite killing insects effectively?
options: It persists in the environment and builds up in food chains
It became too expensive once oil prices rose
Insects stopped being affected by it within a year
Its strong smell made it unusable in homes and farms
quiz.explain: It thinned the eggshells of birds of prey, among other effects.
